articles.title: Waste treatment plants will soon turn wealth generating units, says MA&UD Minister Narayana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Narayana, Minister for Municipal Administration and Urban Development, announced that Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has approved the establishment of 107 waste processing units across the state by July, with an estimated ₹300 crore investment.  The initiative aims to address legacy waste in areas like the Donthali dumping yard in Nellore Rural, where a Jindal group-led waste-to-energy plant is being constructed.

articles.title: Focused on securing best deal, says Piyush Goyal on India-US trade deal | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Piyush Goyal, India's Commerce and Industry Minister, emphasized the government's commitment to securing a favorable trade deal with the United States, stating that he prioritizes achieving the best possible outcome for Indian economic interests. Goyal also highlighted India's expansion of preferential trade discussions with various countries globally, aiming to broaden market access for Indian exporters.  He expressed confidence in India's ability to navigate external shocks due to its robust foreign exchange reserves and significant remittance inflows.

articles.title: Nashik farmers say Rs 15.80/kg rate does not cover input costs | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre has relaxed procurement norms for onions under NAFED (National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd) and NCCF (National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of India Ltd), expanding permissible size limits and easing quality criteria.  However, farmers in Nashik district remain skeptical about the real impact of these changes, citing a significant price gap between market rates and government procurement prices. The Maharashtra government has waived the 0.75 per cent APMC market fee on onion procurement by NAFED and NCCF, but farmers argue that this benefit will not be passed on to growers unless the purchase price is raised accordingly.  Farmers are urging for a minimum procurement price of Rs 30 per kg, citing rising input costs and concerns about delayed procurement impacting their ability to prepare for the next season.

articles.title: Telangana constitutes committee to examine international medical tourism in govt. hospitals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has formed a committee to explore the potential of international medical tourism within its hospitals. The three-member panel, led by Gaurav Uppal from TGMSIDC, will examine feasibility and recommend strategies for establishing dedicated services at TIMS.  They will also suggest patient support systems and marketing initiatives to promote this sector.

articles.title: Separate ELEVATE track for Beyond Bengaluru startups welcomed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government's recent decision to introduce a separate ELEVATE track for startups outside the Bengaluru region has been welcomed by Karnataka Digital Economy Mission’s (KDEM) Mysuru cluster head Sudheer Shankar.  He stated that this change will address concerns about unfair competition between startups in tier 2 and tier 3 regions and Bengaluru-based startups, as ELEVATE previously provided grants to startups in all regions of the state.

articles.title: Global Travel Market 2026 in Kerala clocks over 60,000 B2B meets - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Global Travel Market (GTM 2026) concluded in Thiruvananthapuram, with over 60,000 B2B meetings facilitated. The three-day event saw participation from domestic and international buyers, including 2,000 domestic buyers and 100 international buyers.  The exhibition featured stalls representing leading tourism and hospitality stakeholders from across India, organized by South Kerala Hoteliers Forum (SKHF), Thiruvananthapuram Chamber of Commerce and Industries (TCCI), Thavass Ventures, and Metro Mart, in association with Kerala Tourism and India Tourism.

articles.title: Cotton sowing area likely to rise by 10-15% this kharif season: Officials | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra's agriculture department predicts a 10-15% increase in cotton cultivation areas for the 2026-27 kharif season due to higher market demand and better prices. Farmers, particularly in Vidarbha and Marathwada, are shifting back to cotton from soybean after disappointing yields for soybeans this year.  While cotton prices have surged recently, experts warn that these high prices may not translate into guaranteed returns for farmers due to potential quality issues during procurement and lack of a robust support system.

articles.title: Global airlines slash 2026 profit forecast on fuel shock from Iran war - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has downgraded its 2026 profit forecast for the airline industry to $23 billion, down from a previous projection of $41 billion. This reduction is attributed to soaring jet fuel prices and disruptions in the Gulf region due to the Iran conflict.  Willie Walsh, IATA's Director General, stated that smaller airlines may face bankruptcy or acquisition by larger carriers as higher fuel costs bite. Spirit Airlines was recently shut down due to the conflict, highlighting the impact on the industry. Despite robust passenger demand and rising revenues, airlines are expected to experience a decline in profitability per passenger.

articles.title: Rs 9,49,50,50,00,00,000: Elon Musk's Projected Net Worth And What It Can Buy
articles.rephrased_article: Elon Musk's net worth could soon surpass $1 trillion, according to current projections.  This would make him the first trillionaire and place his wealth larger than many countries around the world. Much of his fortune stems from Tesla stock holdings and options, with an IPO of SpaceX potentially adding another $841 billion. The figure is comparable to the annual economic output of Manhattan and exceeds the combined value of all property in Houston.  Musk's projected wealth surpasses the combined fortunes of several tech billionaires including Jeff Bezos, Larry Ellison, and Larry Page and Sergey Brin.

articles.title: 100 days into Iran war, Americans face higher prices | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The war in Iran has led to increased costs for US consumers, with households spending an average of $750 more on expenses due to the conflict.  This is primarily driven by higher energy prices, which have surged since the start of the conflict. The cost of food has also risen, as fertilizer prices are expected to increase significantly. The Federal Reserve is facing pressure to maintain interest rates at a high level due to inflation caused by the war and other factors.  The Pentagon has requested additional funding for military operations in Iran, with the White House proposing $98 billion in defense spending for fiscal year 2027.

articles.title: Market Trading Guide: Adani Green among 2 stock recommendations for Monday - Stock Ideas | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Domestic equities closed largely flat on Friday, with the RBI's monetary policy outcome matching market expectations.  However, downward revisions in growth forecasts and a calibrated inflation outlook led to profit-taking as investors reassessed near-term demand and earnings prospects. Bonanza Portfolio, through its Senior Technical Research Analyst, Virat Jagad, provided stock recommendations for Monday: Adani Green Energy and Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences.

articles.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide D-Street action on Monday - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The US stock market experienced its worst day since October, driven by a sell-off in technology companies and a strong jobs report. The S&P 500 fell 2.6%, marking its first losing week in the last ten. Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research at Religare Broking, advises caution and prefers a "sell-on-rise" approach until the Nifty reclaims the 23,700 level.  European shares also ended lower due to uncertainty over Middle East peace efforts.

articles.title: Smart money move: Why Groww MF's equity chief is betting on multicap strategies - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Despite recent market corrections, the investment environment for active stock picking in mid and small caps has improved. ET Markets reports that while valuations remain elevated in some areas, a multicap strategy with bottom-up investing can help investors identify opportunities within these segments.  Sectors like financials, industrials, auto, and specialty chemicals offer strong earnings visibility despite market volatility.

articles.title: From the Opinions Editor | Who gets the rupee right: Economists, market wallahs or moralists? | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Economists advocate for an inflation-targeting central bank to focus on controlling inflation rather than defending the rupee. Market wallahs, including some from India Inc., support currency defense measures, citing concerns about capital outflows and market confidence. Moralists propose market interventions and restrictions to punish speculators and curb foreign exchange use. While these groups offer different perspectives, they all agree on the need for facilitating foreign capital flows.

articles.title: One In Six Samples Failed Tests In FY26: Are Indians Losing Faith In Food?
articles.rephrased_article: Nearly one in six food samples tested in India failed safety and quality checks during FY26, according to experts. This trend highlights a growing trust deficit in the country's food ecosystem, with products like milk, paneer, and even snacks becoming subject to adulteration concerns.  Food businesses face pressure to embrace modern quality management systems and transparency to rebuild consumer confidence. Food safety issues are increasingly impacting workplaces, with employees demanding greater transparency from food service providers. Consumers can play a crucial role in protecting themselves by purchasing from licensed vendors, reading labels carefully, and reporting suspected contamination.

articles.title: Most Viewed Business News Articles, Top News Articles | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: FirstCry has been ordered to pay Rs 50,000 in compensation to a customer after cancelling his tricycle order without reason and labeling him a fraud. The consumer commission found FirstCry's defense contradictory.  The company must also refund the customer Rs 2,130 with interest and cover litigation costs. Canada and Mexico have called for the renewal of the North American free trade agreement with the United States, hoping to bind the three countries to a pact that President Donald Trump has questioned.

articles.title: Union Minister Jitendra Singh On Success Of J&K's Bhaderwah Lavender Fields, Breaking Startup Myths
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister Jitendra Singh inaugurated the 4th Lavender Festival in Bhaderwah valley, highlighting significant infrastructure development since 2014 under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership.  He emphasized how lavender cultivation has transformed Bhaderwah into a national hub for aroma-based entrepreneurship and startups, citing PM Modi's vision of "startup India" and science-driven development as key factors in the region's success. He also credited the government's proactive policy changes, particularly after the scrapping of Article 370, for the transformation.  The Union Minister acknowledged the positive impact on the local economy and highlighted the rise of lavender startups despite challenges faced by the community initially.

articles.title: Indian Railways nears 100% electrification: Only 269 Route Km left across 5 states
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Railways has achieved 99.6% electrification of its Broad Gauge network, with only 269 route kilometers remaining across five states.  The Ministry of Railways reports that these final sections are in Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Assam, Karnataka, and Goa. Electrification is crucial for improving train efficiency, reducing fossil fuel dependence, and advancing sustainability goals.

articles.title: AlphaGrep enters MF space, eyes Rs 25,000-30,000 cr AUM in 3-5 yrs; to launch maiden scheme on Jul 6 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: AlphaGrep Investment Management, a global quantitative trading and investment firm, is launching its first mutual fund scheme in India next month. The company aims to reach an asset under management (AUM) of Rs 25,000-30,000 crore over the next three to five years.  The multi-asset allocation fund will open for subscription on July 6 and close on July 20, investing in equity and related instruments, debt, money market instruments, gold, silver, and permitted commodity ETFs. AlphaGrep Investment Management CEO Bhautik Ambani stated the company will focus on quantitative equity and hybrid strategies driven by advanced mathematical models, artificial intelligence, and machine learning.

articles.title: These 8 flexicap funds have low consistency scores. Do you own any? - Low consistency in 5 years | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Canara Robeco, Taurus, Shriram, LIC MF, Axis, SBI, PGIM India, and UTI Mutual Fund funds have low performance consistency scores over the past five years, according to a CRISP Mutual Fund Scorecard.  The funds' risk compared to peers has been low, with investment styles ranging from high momentum to medium quality.  These funds have generated varying returns, with some exceeding 10% CAGR while others falling below 5%.

articles.title: NSE investor accounts cross 26 crore milestone as mobile trading and tier-2/3 cities drive participation - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) reported over 4.3 crore new investor accounts in the past year, representing nearly 17% of its total account base. This growth is attributed to sustained retail interest despite geopolitical uncertainty and market volatility, fueled by initiatives like Investor Awareness Programs and a simplified KYC framework. The exchange's Investor Protection Fund stands at Rs 2,890 crore as of April 30, 2026. Maharashtra leads with the highest number of accounts, followed by Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, West Bengal, and Rajasthan.

articles.title: From Rs 4L to Rs 27L monthly sales in just 9 months: How two marginal farmer brothers built a thriving dairy empire | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Two brothers, Jasveer and Sukhdev Singh, from Punjab have transformed their family farm into a successful dairy processing plant.  The brothers, with the support of their family and local community, invested nearly Rs 1 crore to establish the plant, which now processes over 1,500 litres of milk daily and produces various value-added products like paneer, curd, and ghee. The plant has grown rapidly, generating sales exceeding Rs 27 lakh monthly and achieving a profit margin of over 10 percent.  The family prioritizes debt repayment and expansion while embracing digital marketing to reach customers beyond their region.

articles.title: Equity mutual funds lose up to 10% in a week; international funds emerge as top laggards - Weekly Tracker | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Equity mutual funds experienced significant losses last week, with Mirae Asset Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF FoF being the worst performer at a decline of 9.48%.  The Nasdaq dropped the most among global indices, followed by the S&P 500 and Hang Seng. Funds from PGIM India Mutual Fund, including PGIM India Emerging Markets Equity FoF and PGIM India Global Equity Opp FoF, also saw substantial losses. The decline in equity mutual funds was widespread, with several funds experiencing negative returns ranging from 3.89% to 4.65%.

articles.title: NFO Watch: 2 mutual funds will open for subscription this week. Check dates and key details - Funds in pipeline | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ACE MF and ICICI Prudential are launching two new mutual funds this week. The first, a WOC Aggressive Hybrid Fund, will open for subscription on June 8th and close on June 22nd with a minimum investment of Rs 500.  The second, an ICICI Prudential Nifty Smallcap 250 ETF, will open for subscription on June 9th and close on June 16th with a minimum investment of Rs 1,000. Investors are encouraged to choose funds based on their individual risk tolerance, financial goals, and investment horizon.

articles.title: FIIs, weak global cues among 5 factors that could keep D-St under pressure this week - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex closed 117 points lower on Friday, with losses across various sectors including TCS, Tata Steel, and NTPC.  Global markets were negatively impacted by a strong US jobs report, leading to declines in the Nasdaq, Dow Jones, and S&P 500. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept its policy repo rate unchanged but increased investment limits for NRIs and OCIs.  The market is expected to remain range-bound due to geopolitical tensions, rising inflation concerns, and investor sentiment.

articles.title: FIIs, weak global cues among 5 factors that could keep D-St under pressure this week - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex closed 117 points lower on Friday, with losses across various sectors including Trent, TCS, and Tata Steel.  Global cues from a weaker US market, driven by concerns over rising interest rates and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, impacted investor sentiment. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) maintained its policy repo rate at 5.25%, but raised inflation forecasts and lowered GDP growth projections. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) continued to sell shares, while domestic institutional investors remained net buyers.  The Nifty 50 also closed lower for the second consecutive week, trading within a defined range as markets digested the RBI's policy announcement.

articles.title: Kenyan graduates turn to AI tools for farming as jobs dry up | Agriculture News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kenyan young farmers are turning to AI tools and digital skills to address the lack of formal employment opportunities.  Chepkorir Rotich, a farmer in Kiboito village, uses social media and YouTube to share her farming knowledge and market her produce. Geoffrey Kiprop, another young farmer, utilizes apps like Plantix and Virtual Agronomist to manage his crops and livestock using AI technology. These farmers highlight the importance of passion, consistency, and embracing modern agricultural practices for success in this evolving sector.

articles.title: Saved by the barrel: Why crude hasn't hit the $200 mark - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran, disrupting oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.  Oil prices initially soared above $125 per barrel but have since stabilized near $100 due to alternative supply routes established by oil-producing nations in the Persian Gulf, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. China, the world's largest oil importer, reduced its inbound shipments by nearly 40% in May compared with last year, while the United States increased its crude exports. Market sentiment remains cautious due to expectations of a diplomatic resolution between the US and Iran.

articles.title: Swiggy among 9 largecap stocks with up to 45% upside potential. Do you own any? - Add to Cart! | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Trendlyne, a market data analytics platform, has compiled analyst consensus estimates for BSE large-cap stocks, predicting strong returns over the next 12 months.  Nine stocks are expected to deliver gains of 35% to 45%, with potential upside ranging from 36% to 49%. These include Swiggy, ICICI Prudential, DLF, HDFC Bank, Mahindra & Mahindra, HDFC Life Insurance, Eternal, Lodha Developers, and TCS.  Analysts recommend buying these stocks.

articles.title: US tops India’s LNG basket in May, imports recover to pre-war levels | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: India's LNG imports rebounded in May, exceeding pre-war levels despite a surge in international prices. The US emerged as India's largest source of super-chilled gas, followed by Nigeria, Oman, and Angola.  While major importing countries reduced their LNG intake due to high costs, India prioritized supplies for sectors like city gas distribution, fertilizer, power, and ceramics. Despite the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which disrupted regular LNG flows from key suppliers Qatar and the UAE, alternative sources have helped secure emergency spot cargoes.

articles.title: West Asia conflict: Spot market gas purchases by power plants jump over 300% | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: India's gas-based power generators have significantly increased their natural gas purchases from the spot market this summer due to disruptions in long-term LNG imports. Between April 1 and May 26, these entities purchased a record 44,67,850 million Metric Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu) of natural gas, marking a 336.5% increase compared to the same period in 2025. This surge was driven by limited domestic gas availability and the conflict in West Asia, which has cast a shadow over gas supplies for power plants.  Despite higher spot market prices, these purchases are crucial as gas-based generators play a vital role in meeting evening peak demand during summer months.

articles.title: Pune’s delivery riders demand higher payouts as fuel costs eat into already thin margins | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Zomato and Swiggy delivery partners in Pune are facing increased financial strain due to rising petrol prices.  Parshuram Kamble, a Zomato rider, reports that his daily fuel costs have jumped from Rs 250 to Rs 350, impacting his ability to earn a living. Similarly, Raju Ghube, a Swiggy delivery partner, has seen his fuel expenses increase by over Rs 100 per day, leading to financial difficulties and concerns about the sustainability of his work. These challenges are compounded by platform policies that do not adjust delivery rates despite rising fuel costs, leaving riders with limited options for mitigating their increased expenses.

articles.title: Sense in PM-EAC meeting: Moves to attract foreign funds can get $70 billion | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Prime Minister Narendra Modi led Economic Advisory Council (EAC-PM) meeting on Saturday discussed measures to attract foreign funds, including the removal of taxes on FIIs investing in government bonds and the RBI's initiatives to boost foreign inflows.  These actions are expected to draw around $70 billion in foreign investments, contingent on the inclusion of Indian sovereign debt in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Bond Index. The meeting also addressed concerns about the impact of El Nino and sub-par rainfall, with experts suggesting ways to mitigate India's vulnerability to monsoon vagaries.

articles.title: Amid global uncertainties, PM discusses measures to boost economic growth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired a meeting of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) on Saturday, where members discussed strategies for sustaining and accelerating India's economic growth in light of global uncertainty. The council assessed the potential impact of the ongoing conflict in West Asia on both India and the global economy.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh hosts Creators’ Zone Digital Summit in Amaravati - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Dhatri Reddy, CEO of Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (RTIH) and A.P. Innovation Society (APIS), emphasized the importance of fostering talent and innovation among young creators at the inaugural session of the Creative Zone Digital Summit-2026.  The summit, organized by the Bharat Digital Media Federation (Bharat DMF) in association with RTIH and APIS, featured over 200 participants from across the state who discussed opportunities within the creator ecosystem and the evolving digital landscape. The event also highlighted the potential of the creator economy to generate employment and entrepreneurial opportunities.

articles.title: LPG price hiked by ₹29 per 14.2-kg cylinder - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State-owned fuel retailers have increased the price of domestic LPG by ₹29 per cylinder, marking the second hike in three months. The new price will be ₹942 in Delhi, effective June 7th, and follows a previous increase of ₹60 per cylinder in March due to global energy cost disruptions.  Despite these increases, oil marketing companies continue to sell petrol and diesel below cost, incurring losses on both fuels.

articles.title: South Western Railway plans goods sheds along new lines to boost Karnataka’s regional economies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: South Western Railway (SWR) is planning to establish dedicated railway goods sheds and freight handling infrastructure along newly proposed rail corridors in Karnataka. The initiative aims to reduce dependence on road transport, cut logistics costs, and improve market access for producers. The proposed infrastructure spans several corridors across the state, including Gadag-Wadi, Bagalkot-Kudachi, Ginigera-Raichur, Dharwad–Belagavi, and Tumakuru-Davanagere, which will benefit key agricultural, mining, and industrial regions.  The plan also includes specialized infrastructure for specific commodities like arecanut, maize, timber, and food grains to enhance value chains and strengthen the national supply chain.

articles.title: American builders made houses with puja room, spice kitchen for Indians; Trump aide says 'completely end H-1B visa' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Brandon Gill, a Republican, criticized the housing market decline in Texas attributed to President Trump's crackdown on H-1B visa abuse. CBRE Group, a real estate firm, confirmed that H-1B workers fueled the housing boom between 2018 and present. As Indian buyers are now leaving the market, prices are falling, particularly in Collin County where home prices dropped nearly 9% year-over-year.  The influx of Indian-Americans into Texas has been significant, with Collin and Denton counties becoming some of the fastest-growing areas in the nation.

articles.title: India's Currency Paradox: Cash Is King But Why ATMs Are Drying Up
articles.rephrased_article: India's cash in circulation has nearly tripled since FY17, reaching over Rs 41 lakh crore in FY26. Despite this surge, the number of ATMs has declined from over 2.19 lakh in FY23 to about 2.09 lakh in FY26. The Confederation of ATM Industry (CATMi) has warned of growing stress in the system due to insufficient cash supply gaps and operational challenges.  Banks are facing difficulties with hiring security, maintaining ATMs, and outsourcing services, leading to a shrinking ATM network that may impact rural and semi-urban areas' access to cash.

articles.title: AI will reshape jobs, but India’s bigger challenge is preparing workers, boardrooms and classrooms - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lakshmi Narayanan, Debjani Ghosh, and B. Santhanam discussed the impact of artificial intelligence on India's workforce at The Hindu Huddle's session "I, Robot: How AI is reshaping the future of work." While acknowledging job displacement concerns, they emphasized the need to redesign education, skilling, research, and businesses for an AI-led future. Ghosh suggested a "human sandwich model" where humans frame questions, AI performs tasks, and humans verify outcomes.  Santhanam highlighted India's potential in AI diffusion across sectors like agriculture, education, and healthcare, but criticized the lack of technology understanding among corporate boards and insufficient investment in research. Narayanan agreed that India needs to invest more in innovation and research to become a leader in shaping the next wave of AI.

articles.title: Delhi Infra Body Extends Booking Deadline For Karkardooma Housing Scheme
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) extended the booking period for its premium housing project, "DDA Towering Heights at East Delhi Hub, Karkardooma Housing Scheme 2026," until June 30, 2026. The scheme offers 741 two-bedroom flats on a first-come, first-served basis with prices ranging from Rs 1.85 crore to Rs 2.10 crore.  The project is attracting interest due to its location, connectivity, and DDA ownership credentials. Buyers can apply through the DDA's Awaas Portal before the deadline.

articles.title: 'Beer should be better in 2026': WC to boost global sales by a billion pints
articles.rephrased_article: A study by Jefferies, an investment bank, predicts that the 2026 FIFA World Cup will boost global beer consumption by one billion pints. The expanded tournament format with more matches and games in favorable time zones is expected to drive increased sales, particularly for companies like Anheuser-Busch InBev and Heineken.  The economic impact of the event, including tourism and GDP growth, is projected to be significant but may not have lasting effects.

articles.title: RBI Examining "Pros And Cons" Of Plastic Currency Notes, No Decision Yet
articles.rephrased_article: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that the central bank is reviewing a proposal to introduce polymer or plastic currency notes, but no final decision has been made.  The RBI is assessing the advantages and challenges of this potential change before deciding on its implementation.  Malhotra assured that sufficient currency stock is available for ATMs and bank branches, and the central bank is prepared to respond quickly to any localized shortages.

articles.title: Telangana woos Malaysian investors in semi-conductor sector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Duddilla Sridhar Babu, Minister of IT and Industries for Telangana, met with a Malaysian delegation led by Deputy Chief Minister II, YB Jagdeep Singh Deo. The meeting focused on potential collaborations between the two states in areas such as semiconductors, electronics manufacturing, and AI.  Sridhar Babu emphasized Hyderabad's growing role as an international hub for advanced technologies and highlighted the state's potential in various sectors. Jagdeep Singh Deo expressed Penang's interest in collaborating with Telangana to deepen cooperation and develop a comprehensive action plan.

articles.title: Abnormal rise in price of cotton yarn hits the textile industry in Karur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The price of cotton yarn has surged in Karur, impacting the textile industry. Industry sources report a 30% to 40% increase due to geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran, disrupting global trade and shipping.  The Centre removed import duty on cotton yarn but this did not help textile manufacturers in Karur as prices remain high. The Karur Textile Manufacturers and Exporters Association has requested government intervention to stabilize yarn prices.

articles.title: Share of Russian oil in Indian imports rises to 38%, premium paid jumps 425% in April 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's oil imports rebounded in April 2026, reaching 195.3 lakh tonnes after a dip in March. However, the surge in oil prices led to a significant increase in India's import bill, rising 61.3% to $15.4 billion. Russia's share of India's oil imports jumped to nearly 38%, marking an 11-month high, while India's reliance on oil from the U.S. fell to multi-month lows.  The premium for Russian oil increased by 425% in April compared to March.

articles.title: ‘I now earn ₹40,000 a month’: How women are riding autos and bikes to build livelihoods in Telangana - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Women Safety Wing launched Stree Ride, an initiative aimed at training and employing women as drivers and riders in the transportation sector.  The program provided 55 women with driver training and employment support through partnerships with mobility service providers and aggregators. Stree Ride aims to address safety concerns by connecting women with opportunities in passenger transportation while increasing female participation in the workforce. The initiative seeks to create jobs, challenge stereotypes, and improve women's economic independence.

articles.title: PM Narendra Modi Chairs Key Economic Advisory Council Meeting Amid Iran War
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with members of the Economic Advisory Council (EAC) on Saturday to discuss strategies for boosting India's economic growth amidst global uncertainty.  The meeting focused on reforms aimed at improving ease of living and doing business, according to official sources. The EAC-PM members also assessed the impact of the ongoing conflict in West Asia on both India and the world.

articles.title: Modest growth in State’s Own Tax Revenue emerges as weak spot in T.N.’s economy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu experienced a modest economic growth rate of 10.83% in 2025-26, but its State Own Tax Revenue (SOTR) growth was only 6.8%.  The increase in SOTR to ₹1.92 lakh crore from ₹1.80 lakh crore was attributed to the GST rate rationalization implemented in September 2022 and below-par compliance among traders. The Finance Minister, Thangam Thennarasu, had anticipated a revenue shortfall of around ₹9,600 crore for 2025-26 due to this issue.  However, an economist believes that consumption will eventually boost tax collections once the economic growth is driven by exports or broad-based activities.

articles.title: Paddy procurement deal with public sector banks renewed, says Kerala Agriculture Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T. Siddique, Kerala Minister for Agriculture, announced that the UDF government renewed its agreement with public sector banks for paddy procurement in the state. The agreement will continue to allow Supplyco to procure paddy from growers and repay bank loans, though delays have been a recurring issue. A sub-committee formed by the UDF government addressed concerns about paddy procurement, including moisture content and crop loss compensation, aiming to complete the process before monsoon.

articles.title: Oil India’s latest gas find could unlock more hydrocarbon reserves in Andaman offshore | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: OIL India Ltd. announced its second natural gas discovery in the Andaman offshore region, located around 15 kilometers off the eastern coast of the Andaman Islands. The discovery was made at the Vijayapuram-3 exploratory well and follows a previous gas strike at the Vijayapuram-2 well. Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri expressed optimism about the basin's potential as a key hydrocarbon-producing zone, highlighting India’s growing success in offshore exploration efforts. Industry experts believe these discoveries could encourage further exploration and appraisal work to assess the region’s hydrocarbon potential.

articles.title: US stocks slump as fears over Big Tech shake Wall Street
articles.rephrased_article: US stock markets experienced a significant decline on Friday, with the Nasdaq index suffering its largest one-day drop since April 2025. The strong US jobs report, which fueled fears of sustained high interest rates, contributed to the selloff.  David Doyle, head of economics at Macquarie Group, suggested that the figures were "too good" and likely to lead to further rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. Investors shifted away from tech stocks, favoring safer investments like healthcare and consumer staples. President Donald Trump criticized the market's reaction to the positive jobs report, arguing that it should be viewed as a sign of economic strength.

articles.title: Assam cabinet Hikes Dearness Allowance To 60 percent, Over 8 Lakh Employees, pensioners To Benefit
articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Cabinet approved a 2-percentage-point increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR) for state government employees, raising it from 58% to 60%. The cabinet also increased the MLA Local Area Development (MLALAD) allocation from Rs 1 crore to Rs 1.5 crore per MLA for FY 2026-27 and Rs 2 crore from FY 2027-28. Additionally, Assam declared Dibrugarh as its Second State Capital Region with a new Development Authority.

articles.title: India defies West Asia war concerns as Q4 GDP growth hits 7.8%; risks remain ahead - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: GDP growth surprised on the upside for Q4, expanding 8% in the December quarter, exceeding expectations of 7.3%. The Reserve Bank of India revised its FY27 growth forecast downward to 6.6%, citing the impact of the ongoing war and a weaker monsoon.  Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that the government is committed to maintaining economic momentum despite global challenges. ICRA chief economist Aditi Nayar noted that the economy did not experience significant impact from the conflict, while HDFC Bank principal economist Sakshi Gupta attributed the growth primarily to private investments and consumption.

articles.title: Central bank turns piper to draw in foreign capital; leaves repo rate at 5.25, keeps stance neutral - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RBI took several measures to attract foreign investment, including incentives for public sector units to raise external commercial borrowings and support for fresh three-to-five-year FCNR(B) deposits. The central bank revised its inflation forecast upward to 5.1% and lowered its growth projection for FY27 to 6.6%. Sanjay Malhotra, governor of the RBI, stated that these measures are expected to support the rupee, which has fallen since the start of the US-Iran conflict.  Economists anticipate inflows of at least $40 billion and a potential pullback in the rupee toward 92-93 levels.

articles.title: Reform, perform, transform will go on: PM Modi hails 7.7% GDP growth | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed India's estimated 7.7% GDP growth for the 2025-26 fiscal year as "good news," emphasizing the country's resilience during a global economic crisis. Modi stated that India will continue its path of reform, performance, and transformation at a fast pace, highlighting the strength of the Indian economy. He acknowledged the collective efforts of 140 crore citizens in managing and exceeding expectations amidst global challenges.

articles.title: Can Supriya Life Sciences unlock its next leg of growth beyond APIs? | Smart Stocks News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Supriya Life Sciences, an API manufacturer, is transitioning from a traditional API business to a broader pharmaceutical player. The company focuses on products where Chinese manufacturers dominate supply, positioning itself as an alternative supplier for regulated markets.  This strategy includes expanding into formulations, contrast media APIs, and contract manufacturing services. While the Ambernath facility represents a significant expansion, Supriya's growth is driven by multiple initiatives rather than a single project. The company faces execution risks related to commercialization timelines, customer qualification, and competition from Chinese manufacturers. Investors are evaluating Supriya based on its existing API business but will need to assess the success of these new initiatives in the coming years.

articles.title: Moving fast to close ‘open-ends’; first tranche of India-US trade deal by mid-July: Piyush Goyal | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Piyush Goyal, India's Commerce Minister, announced that the country and the US will sign the initial phase of their trade agreement by mid-July.  Donald Trump, US President, stated that a deal is in progress and he has confidence in the relationship between the two countries. The Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) led a delegation to India from June 1st to 4th to discuss the trade agreement. Experts warn that Section 301 tariffs are more powerful than previous measures, giving the USTR wide powers to impose restrictions and retaliate against unfair trade practices.

articles.title: Under PM Modi, India’s economy resilient and showing sustained growth: BJP chief - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nitin Nabin, president of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), stated that India's economy continues to demonstrate resilience and growth under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  He attributed this success to a 7.7% GDP growth rate in FY 2025-26 and 7.8% growth in Q4 of the same fiscal year, highlighting broad-based growth across sectors. Nabin emphasized that these figures strengthen investment, create opportunities for youth, and enhance ease of living for citizens, further supporting India's progress towards the vision of "Viksit Bharat 2047".

articles.title: US stocks today: Nasdaq crashes 1,100 pts, Dow 600 pts as chip stocks slide; jobs data fuels rate hike fears - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S. stock market experienced a sharp decline on Friday, with the Nasdaq Composite Index suffering its largest one-day percentage loss since last year. Nvidia, Intel, and other chip stocks fell sharply as investors reacted to strong job growth and concerns about rising interest rates and inflation. The S&P 500 ended its nine-week winning streak, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped by 1.33%.  The robust jobs report fueled speculation of a Fed rate hike in December, further dampening investor sentiment.

articles.title: Trump makes pitch to farmers hard-hit by tariffs, high prices in Wisconsin | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump visited Wisconsin to address concerns of farmers impacted by tariffs and the economic fallout from the US-Israel war with Iran.  He sought to bolster support for Republican US Representative Derrick Van Orden, who has aligned himself with Trump's agenda. Trump assured farmers that the administration was "largely finished" with the war and promised lower fertilizer and gas prices. The visit comes amidst low approval ratings for Trump, as several Republicans have expressed concerns about his recent actions potentially alienating voters concerned about the economy.

articles.title: India can regain 7% growth by FY28: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nageswaran, Secretary of the Indian Ministry of Finance, stated that India's GDP growth is projected at 7% in FY28, assuming a return to pre-February 2023 global conditions.  He attributed this growth to structural reforms and government investments in infrastructure. However, RBI lowered its GDP forecast for FY27 to 6.6%, citing higher energy prices and supply disruptions linked to the Iran war.  Nageswaran also noted that domestic demand remains resilient but warned of potential risks from global uncertainty, including inflation and weather patterns.

articles.title: Govt to tap AI for mapping supply chains and investment clusters - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NCAER workshop attendees heard that India's government is prioritizing data harmonization as a key aspect of its digital public infrastructure strategy.  Ashwini Vaishnaw, the Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, emphasized the importance of high-quality data in driving AI development. He stressed that while APIs and platforms facilitate information exchange between ministries, achieving "semantic interoperability" is crucial to ensure consistent data across datasets.

articles.title: Trump admin’s cancellation of wind energy projects causes business turmoil | Renewable Energy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration canceled several offshore wind energy projects, causing turmoil for developers and states. TotalEnergies, a French energy giant, agreed to withdraw from four leases in exchange for payments totaling over $2 billion. Seven northeastern states are suing the government, arguing that the cancellation was arbitrary and detrimental to their energy needs. The Interior Department cited security concerns as justification, but the lawsuit claims these concerns were already addressed before awarding the leases. TotalEnergies maintains it withdrew due to cost considerations and believes the technology is not yet suitable for the US market. This action has raised concerns about investment predictability in renewable energy under a new administration and could impact future offshore wind projects.

articles.title: This Summer Travel Season Could Forever Alter the Future of Sustainable Aviation Fuel | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Miller, a Vancouver-based aviation analyst, and his family canceled their summer trip to Rome due to the global fuel shortage caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The situation has led to rising jet fuel prices and flight cancellations across various airlines. United Airlines, Delta, American Airlines, and Cathay Pacific are among those using sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), which can cut emissions by up to 80 percent, but currently costs more than conventional jet fuel.  The industry is hopeful that SAF will help bridge the gap between rising prices and increased demand for summer travel. World Energy, a US conglomerate, previously produced SAF but has scaled back production due to resource constraints. However, recent events have highlighted the need for alternative fuels like SAF.

articles.title: US adds 172,000 jobs in May, easing fears of labour market slowdown
articles.rephrased_article: The US economy added 172,000 jobs in May, exceeding economists' expectations of 85,000. This robust performance suggests a resilient labor market despite geopolitical tensions and higher oil prices.  However, the gains are attributed to companies holding onto employees rather than aggressive hiring, driven by concerns about tariffs and uncertainty surrounding the US-Israeli war with Iran. The Federal Reserve is expected to maintain its key interest rate at current levels for the foreseeable future, keeping borrowing costs elevated despite a stable job market.

articles.title: Quant Smallcap among 16 equity mutual funds that multiply lumpsum investments by over 2.3x in 5 years - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Motilal Oswal Midcap Fund was the top performer, with a 2.58 times return on a Rs 1 lakh investment over five years.  Other funds that saw significant growth include Nippon India Mutual Fund's Nippon India Growth Mid Cap Fund and Nippon India Small Cap Fund, which both multiplied investments by 2.50 times.  Several other mutual funds also achieved strong returns, including HDFC Mid Cap Fund, Invesco India Smallcap Fund, and HSBC Midcap Fund, with some exceeding a 2.3 times return.

articles.title: Quant Smallcap among 16 equity mutual funds that multiply lumpsum investments by over 2.3x in 5 years - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Motilal Oswal Midcap Fund was the top performer, with a 2.58 times return on a Rs 1 lakh investment over five years. Nippon India Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, and other funds also saw significant growth, with returns ranging from 2.17% to 2.58%. The analysis was conducted to identify mutual funds that multiplied investments by 2.3 times in the last five years, but it is not a recommendation for investment decisions.

articles.title: Oyo parent Prism Hotels receives Sebi nod for IPO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Prism, the rebranded parent entity of a travel and hospitality company, has received approval from Sebi to proceed with an initial public offering (IPO). The IPO is expected to raise $7–8 billion in fresh equity shares, aiming to strengthen its balance sheet, expand into new markets, and achieve profitability.  The listing is seen as a sign of renewed investor interest in technology-driven consumer internet companies in India after a period of subdued IPO activity.

articles.title: India makes big moves to attract foreign investments in bonds: How will this impact stock market? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's government exempted foreign institutional investors (FIIs) from capital gains tax on investments in government securities, and also announced measures to boost FPI investments. The RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra unveiled a series of measures to attract more foreign investment, including expanding the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) for government bonds and raising investment limits for NRIs and OCIs in equity instruments. These announcements aim to broaden participation in Indian capital markets and support liquidity and inflows.  Analysts suggest caution as the RBI maintains its hawkish policy stance despite easing short-term market volatility.

articles.title: Unicorn in the USA: Indians aren't stealing American jobs; they are building entire HR departments - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new report by the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP) highlights the significant contributions of immigrants to the US startup ecosystem. The study reveals that immigrants have founded or co-founded 455 out of America's 775 unicorns, accounting for 59% of all billion-dollar startups. Notably, people of Indian origin lead the unicorn league table with 96 billion-dollar companies, surpassing other immigrant groups like Israel and China. The report challenges xenophobic narratives against immigrants by showcasing their entrepreneurial success and economic impact on the US economy.

articles.title: Data Centre Specialist AirTrunk To Invest Rs 3 Lakh Crore In India: PM Modi
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that AirTrunk, a hyperscale data centre specialist, plans to invest over Rs 3 lakh crore (USD 30 billion) in India by 2030. This investment will support the development of 5 GW of data centre capacity and strengthen India's position as a global hub for cloud computing and AI. AirTrunk CEO Robin Khuda expressed excitement about supporting Modi's vision for India's digital economy, which has attracted significant foreign investment, including backing from Blackstone and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.

articles.title: Has Microsoft Lost Its Mojo (Again)? | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Consumers in Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia, Utah, Oregon, Texas, Montana, Delaware, Iowa, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Tennessee, Minnesota, Maryland, Indiana, Kentucky, and Rhode Island have the right to opt-out of targeted advertising. Companies use personal information to serve ads believed to be of interest to consumers, according to their privacy policy. Consumers can opt out by toggling a "Allow Targeted Advertising" option or submitting a request through the company's privacy center or by calling 1-877-241-4999.

articles.title: Satellite Data Shows Iran War-Led Slowdown In India's Major Industrial Hubs
articles.rephrased_article: Indian industrial clusters, particularly in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Uttar Pradesh, experienced reduced nitrogen dioxide emissions due to disruptions caused by the Middle East war.  Satellite data analysis by NDTV Datafy, using data from the European Space Agency's Sentinel-5P, revealed lower NO2 levels during March-May 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. This decline is attributed to reduced production capacity due to fuel and export challenges, as well as higher input costs for raw materials and fuel.  Jitendra P Vakharia, president of the South Gujarat Textile Processors Association, reported that many textile manufacturers had reduced production due to these factors, while KJ Kundariya, former president of Morbi Ceramic Association, noted similar issues in the ceramic industry.

articles.title: The DOGE Boys Get VC Funding to Support Their Latest Enterprise | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Former members of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), including Nate Cavanaugh and Justin Fox, have launched a startup called Special with backing from venture capital firm a16z. The company aims to use AI to transform critical American industries by vertically integrating businesses in sectors like senior care, construction, and manufacturing.  Special's work is reminiscent of DOGE's practices, which included allegations of fraud and waste at government agencies, and has attracted investors including billionaire Elon Musk's right-hand man Steve Davis and Coinbase founder Brian Armstrong. However, critics argue that the company relies on narrow perspectives on government issues and may have ties to questionable past actions by its founders.

articles.title: India makes big moves to attract foreign investments in bonds: How will this impact stock market? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's government removed capital gains tax on investments by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in government securities and exempted them from tax on interest income and capital gains. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also unveiled measures to boost FPI investments, including expanding the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) for government bonds and raising investment limits for NRIs and OCIs in listed equity instruments. These moves are expected to attract more foreign capital inflows and support market depth, liquidity, and long-term capital inflows.  Analysts believe these initiatives will provide short-term support for the Indian stock market but caution against the RBI's hawkish policy stance.

articles.title: Hospitality jobs boom as US prepares for World Cup
articles.rephrased_article: The US economy added 172,000 jobs in May, driven by growth in leisure and hospitality, local government, and healthcare. Fifa is facing scrutiny for allegedly inflating ticket prices ahead of the World Cup, while concerns are growing that rising costs will dampen economic gains.  Despite strong job numbers, economists predict an interest rate hike later this year due to increasing inflation caused by the US-Israel war in Iran.

articles.title: Unicorn in the USA: Indians aren't stealing American jobs; they are building entire HR departments - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new policy brief by the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP) highlights the significant contributions of immigrants to the US economy, particularly in the booming tech sector. The report states that immigrants have founded or co-founded 455 out of America's 775 unicorns, representing 59% of all billion-dollar startups.  This success is attributed to immigrant founders and their teams, with Indian-origin individuals leading the charge, contributing significantly to the nation's economic growth. Notably, the report challenges the narrative of immigrants stealing jobs, showcasing the positive impact of immigrant entrepreneurship on both the US economy and individual wealth.

articles.title: Titan Company shares gain 2%. Why JPMorgan, others see up to 28% upside after analyst call? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Titan Company, a Tata Group company, outlined ambitious growth targets for the next five years, aiming to double both its consolidated revenue and EBIT.  Analysts from JPMorgan, Motilal Oswal, and JM Financial have all issued positive ratings on Titan shares, citing factors such as structural growth drivers in the jewellery market, strong brand recognition, and diversification into non-jewellery businesses. Despite near-term challenges posed by rising gold prices and regulatory changes, analysts believe Titan remains well positioned for long-term success.

articles.title: Tata Steel shares fall 3% after fire breaks out at UK’s Port Talbot plant - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Steel UK reported a fire at its Port Talbot site on Thursday, prompting emergency services to remain at the scene. The fire was contained and is not related to the demolition of an empty gas holder earlier in the day. Mid and West Wales Fire Service attended the incident alongside local teams, while Tata Steel UK confirmed all personnel were evacuated safely.  The company is transitioning the site to an electric arc furnace with a £1.25 billion investment, expected to be completed by 2027.

articles.title: Hindustan Zinc shares tumble 5% to 6-week low after report of govt's plan to sell 2% stake for Rs 5,000 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta and Hindustan Zinc share prices dropped following a Bloomberg report indicating the government's potential stake sale in Hindustan Zinc. The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) aims to launch this process this month or in July.  The government is also considering an OFS to sell 2% stake in LIC, aiming to raise Rs 10,000 crore.  Vedanta confirmed that the Enforcement Directorate visited some of its offices, but no penalty was imposed. The company's shares have declined significantly in recent weeks and months.

articles.title: Panic In Silicon Valley: Why 15,000 Indians Fled US Last Year - And More Are On Their Way
articles.rephrased_article: Over 15,000 Indian tech professionals returned to India in 2025 and 7,300 have already done so this year due to a combination of factors including visa denials, layoffs, and the job market's shift towards AI. The US government's decision to increase H-1B visa fees has also contributed to the exodus, as many companies are now choosing to hire local workers instead.  The Trump administration's policies have created resentment among some Americans who believe Indian professionals are taking American jobs, while others argue that these professionals help boost job prospects for Americans. The situation is further complicated by the growing use of AI and corporate restructuring within tech giants like Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, which has led to mass layoffs and a shrinking job market for Indian tech professionals.  Despite efforts from US tech giants to invest in India, the number of returning professionals exceeds their capacity to absorb them.

articles.title: $27.6 Billion: Behind Centre's Tax Relief To Foreign Investors On G-Secs
articles.rephrased_article: India's government has exempted foreign investors from taxes on interest income and capital gains earned from government securities to attract more global capital into the debt market. This move, experts believe, will boost foreign inflows, deepen the bond market, support the rupee, and improve liquidity in government securities. The tax relief is seen as a positive signal for India's financial architecture and its standing in global capital markets, potentially attracting sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, and other large institutional investors seeking stable investment avenues backed by sovereign credit.

articles.title: India Reports GDP Growth Of 7.8% In Q4 On Services Sector Output Boost
articles.rephrased_article: India's real GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, exceeding market expectations and contributing to full-year growth of 7.7%. The secondary and tertiary sectors drove this growth, with the secondary sector expanding 8.8% and the tertiary sector growing 9.3%.  The BJP praised these figures, calling them a testament to India's economic strength while Rahul Gandhi, a Congress leader, warned of an "economic tsunami."

articles.title: CG Power's growth momentum strong, but valuation comfort missing: Sandip Sabharwal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: CG Power recently inaugurated its S3 unit in Nashik, doubling its switchgear production capacity. While the expansion reflects strong demand trends in the power equipment segment, analyst Sandip Sabharwal cautions that valuations for companies like CG Power, Hitachi Energy, and GE Vernova have become significantly high, exceeding traditional fair value measures. He suggests investors who bought these stocks at lower levels should hold on but new investors should wait for corrections before entering the market.  Sabharwal also notes that while pharmaceutical company Wockhardt's Zaynich approval is a positive development, near-term upside may be limited due to the time needed for commercialization and market development. In the aviation sector, airlines are scaling back certain international operations due to elevated fuel costs and weak seasonal demand, but stronger players like InterGlobe Aviation are expected to emerge with enhanced competitive positioning.

articles.title: Go Digit Insurance shares jump 9% after Rs 100 crore block deal attracts MFs, global investor - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund and JPMorgan (Taiwan) Eastern Technology Fund acquired a significant stake in Go Digit Insurance, purchasing 33.33 lakh shares at Rs 300 per share for approximately Rs 100 crore. The seller was Peak XV Partners Growth Investments III, who offloaded its entire stake. Despite recent market fluctuations, Go Digit Insurance's financial performance has been strong, with revenue and net profit both showing significant growth in the March 2026 quarter.  The stock's price has increased following a large block deal, but it remains below key long-term resistance levels.

articles.title: Rupee rises 50 paise to 95.24 against US dollar post RBI policy decision - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a policy that boosted investor confidence, with the rupee strengthening against the US dollar. The RBI kept interest rates unchanged and raised investment limits for NRIs in equity instruments.  Brent crude prices rose, while the dollar index increased slightly. Domestic equities experienced losses, with the Sensex and Nifty declining.

articles.title: Vedanta demerger: How will the mega restructuring impact dividend payouts for shareholders? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta announced a major corporate restructuring in April, demerging its subsidiaries into four separate companies: Vedanta Aluminium Metal (VAML), Vedanta Power, Vedanta Oil and Gas, and Vedanta Iron and Steel. The move resulted in a significant share price drop on the record date, May 1st.  Analysts predict that while Vedanta will continue to be a dividend-paying entity, its overall dividend payout may decrease due to the carve-out of cash-generating businesses. Investors are advised to evaluate each new company's free cash flow generation and growth appetite before making investment decisions.

articles.title: Capital flow push: RBI eases foreign borrowing rules for PSUs, FCNR deposits of banks | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a series of measures to attract capital inflows and bolster the rupee. These include relaxing norms on overseas borrowing for public sector firms, encouraging foreign currency deposit mobilization by banks, and providing concessional forex swap facilities until September 2026. The RBI also expanded the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) for foreign institutional investors, increased investment limits for NRIs and OCIs in equity instruments, and restored the export realization period to nine months. These measures are expected to strengthen India's balance of payments and attract capital inflows.

articles.title: Government Bond Returns Now Tax-Free For Foreign Investors
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government issued the Income Tax Amendment Ordinance, 2026, to exempt foreign institutional investors (FIIs) from paying taxes on interest income and capital gains from Indian government securities. The ordinance, effective April 1, 2026, reduces long-term capital gains tax on G-Secs to zero and eliminates withholding tax on interest income. This move aims to attract global capital and strengthen India's position as a leading investment destination.  The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is also included in the exemption.

articles.title: The Motley Fool Promo Code: $200 Off on Stock Advisor June 2026 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: The Motley Fool, a long-standing investment advice website founded in the early 1990s by brothers Tom and David Gardner, offers various subscription tiers with stock tips and analysis services. The three main tiers are Stock Advisor ($199), Epic ($499), and Epic Plus ($1,999).  The site's most popular option, Stock Advisor, provides market-beating "Top 10 Stocks to Buy Now" plus portfolio analysis, analyst news, and monthly stock rankings. Motley Fool also offers a money-back guarantee on all new plans for 30 days.

articles.title: Credit guarantee scheme for MFIs still stuck in low gear - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NBFC-MFIs are anticipating a surge in loan disbursement from banks following the credit guarantee scheme's scheduled closure on June 30.  The scheme, launched in March, has received an aggregate loan demand of Rs 10,000-12,500 crore, but rigid caps on lending rates and margin rules have hindered its effectiveness. While large NBFC-MFIs are expected to benefit from the program, smaller MFIs may face challenges securing funding without bank support.  Despite the guarantee cover, banks will maintain strict underwriting standards for borrowers, potentially impacting loan disbursement for financially weaker companies.

articles.title: The curious case of Rajesh Exports: Massive revenues, meagre profits - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has accused REL, a company owned by its chairman, Rajesh Mehta, of committing financial fraud. The regulator found that REL inflated its revenue by booking personal gold trades as corporate sales and using funds from the company to benefit the promoter.  REL denies these allegations, claiming confusion with Valcambi SA's Ebitda figures. Sebi also criticized the company's auditors for not providing necessary documents and statements during their investigation. The company's market cap was just over ₹3,000 crore as of Thursday.

articles.title: FPI exodus from financials cools, but foreign investors remain net sellers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) sold shares worth ₹5,181 crore from the sector in the second half of May, a significant decrease compared to the first half's outflows. This follows a trend of sustained selling pressure throughout 2023, with FPIs offloading equities worth over ₹2.6 lakh crore so far this year, exceeding their outflow of ₹1.7 lakh crore in 2025. The sell-off is attributed to factors like AI disruption and inflationary pressures, leading to a decline in net foreign investment in Indian equities to the lowest level in 12 years.

articles.title: Sensex rises over 200 points, Nifty above 23,450 as investors eye RBI MPC meet outcome - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 closed higher today, driven by gains in sectors like IT and consumer durables.  Infosys, UltraTech Cement, TCS, and other companies led the positive momentum. However, Tata Steel saw losses on the benchmark index. The Rupee strengthened against the US dollar, gaining 8 paise to 95.66. Foreign investors remained net sellers of Indian equities, contributing to a bearish sentiment in the market.  The focus for the day will be on the RBI's monetary policy announcement and its implications for future interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Adani Ports shares snap 2-day fall, rise over 1% after Goldman Sachs raises target price - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Goldman Sachs highlighted that cargo volumes in May 2026 rose 16% year-on-year to 48.3 million tonnes, driven by increases in liquid cargo and container volumes. Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 3,329 crore for the March-ended quarter, marking a 10% increase year-on-year. The company's revenue grew 26% year-on-year to Rs 10,737 crore in Q4FY26, and its EBITDA increased by 20% year-on-year.

articles.title: Sensex Today, Stock Market LIVE Updates | Nifty | Share Market: Sensex Jumps 250 Points Amid Mixed Global Cues
articles.rephrased_article: Indian equity benchmarks opened in green on Friday, driven by investor optimism despite the ongoing US-Iran situation. The RBI is set to announce its decision on the repo rate today.  The Nifty 50 closed nearly flat at 23,416.55, while the Sensex jumped 250 points. Experts predict a stable real estate sector due to the RBI's decision to maintain the repo rate at 5.25%. The crypto market remains under pressure as risk appetite weakens and volatility expands across major assets.

articles.title: IndiGo suspends operations to 6 international destinations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: IndiGo, India's largest airline, announced the temporary suspension of services to six international destinations, including Hong Kong and Krabi, starting July 1. The decision is attributed to a softer demand in the upcoming quarter and challenging cost environments, with the airline aiming to resume bookings on October 1st. IndiGo maintains over 1,800 weekly international flights despite this realignment.

articles.title: IndiGo suspends operations to 6 international destinations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: IndiGo, India’s largest airline, announced the temporary suspension of flights to six international destinations starting July 1st. The budget carrier cited a softer demand in the upcoming quarter and challenging operating costs as reasons for the decision.  The affected destinations include Hong Kong, Krabi, Ho Chi Minh City, Langkawi, Shanghai, and Siem Reap. IndiGo will resume bookings for these routes on October 1st, subject to market conditions improving. The airline maintains over 1,800 weekly international flights despite the realignment.

articles.title: India’s long-term growth story intact despite high valuations: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Fraser, chief economist at BofA Global Research, believes India's long-term economic prospects remain strong despite current headwinds.  The recent pullback by foreign portfolio investors is a pause in reassessment of financial assets, geopolitical risks, and monetary policy. While valuations are high compared to some alternatives, Fraser emphasizes that this does not reflect a weaker Indian economy but rather different valuation metrics. The world's shift towards multipolarity will benefit India, while cybersecurity poses a significant risk.

articles.title: BIT sweeter? India weighs easing treaty rules with safeguards to attract foreign capital - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's government is considering relaxing the five-year timeline for foreign investors to exhaust legal remedies before pursuing arbitration under its investment treaties. The government is also weighing granting "most-favored nation" (MFN) forward benefits, but safeguards will be implemented to prevent abuse of treaty terms. These decisions will be made after broader consultations and are part of a larger effort to attract sustained foreign investments amid concerns over capital outflows and the need for strategic technology investments.

articles.title: First chilled seafood export to Oman flagged off from Chennai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Aqua World Exports Pvt. Ltd., an Indian seafood exporter, shipped the first chilled fish consignment under the India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to Oman. The shipment was flagged off at the Chennai Air Cargo Complex and facilitated by Lulu Logistics, with participation from officials of the Export Inspection Agency (EIA) and the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA).  Oman is becoming a key market for Indian seafood exports, with shipments expected to increase significantly.

articles.title: Chief Minister Vijay reviews functioning of Natural Resources Department - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, convened a meeting with officials to discuss the proper and sustainable use of mineral resources and prevent illegal transportation. The review focused on the functioning of the Department of Geology and Mining, efforts to make Tamil Nadu a leading state in mineral resource management, and the use of modern technologies to combat illegal mining.  The meeting also addressed increasing revenue from mineral extraction.

articles.title: Nicobar port has no ‘strategic goals’, Finance Ministry body said in 2024 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Public Investment Board (PIB) previously deemed the proposed International Container Transhipment Port (ICTP) at Galathea Bay as lacking strategic objectives. Despite this shift in narrative, the project has faced scrutiny from environmental groups and opposition from Congress MP Jairam Ramesh who argues that the project is primarily a commercial venture. articles.title: Agri Ministry’s platform for farmers, Mahakumbh 2025 among e-governance award winners | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Union government awarded 16 projects across the country with National Awards for e-Governance, recognizing excellence in digital governance initiatives. The awards were presented in seven categories, including a special recognition for deepening service delivery at grassroots level through digitization. Projects like the Agri Stack platform by the Agriculture Ministry, and the e-Jagriti portal by the Consumer Affairs Ministry were among the winners.

articles.title: Under SEBI scanner, Rajesh Exports claims revenues ‘correct’, cites ‘confusion and communication gap’ | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rajesh Exports, a gold jewellery retailer, defended its financial filings against an interim order from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) alleging misrepresentation of revenue. articles.rephrased_article: The White House announced a plan to impose tariffs on 60 economies, citing concerns about forced labor in goods trade. articles.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit: Rajeev Thakkar of PPFAS MF explains when to hold, when to exit, and why most investors get it wrong - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Thakkar, CIO and Director at PPFAS Asset Management, emphasized the importance of long-term investing, stating that investors should avoid selling stocks based on short-term fluctuations or news flow. He cautioned against "profit booking" and highlighted the detrimental effects of frequent buying and selling on compounding returns.  Thakkar stressed the need for patience with strong businesses and diversification to mitigate risk. Investors should acknowledge mistakes early and exit positions when necessary, such as due to structural disruption or excessive valuations. Thakkar also recommended a phased approach to selling, gradually reducing exposure rather than making large transactions. He emphasized that successful investing is about avoiding unnecessary activity and maintaining long-term portfolios for compounding returns.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow soars 800 points to hit record as Iran optimism offsets chip slump, weak jobs data - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged to a record closing high, boosted by gains in healthcare and financial stocks.  However, the Nasdaq Composite ended essentially unchanged, with chipmaker Broadcom missing revenue expectations, sending its shares tumbling. The U.S. House of Representatives passed a measure blocking President Trump from continuing the war on Iran, while a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon offered optimism for a near-term resolution to the conflict.  Despite these positive developments, initial jobless claims unexpectedly rose, and first-quarter labor costs and productivity were revised lower.

articles.title: Citi initiates coverage on 4 Indian power equipment stocks; sees up to 33% upside. Own any? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Citigroup initiated "Buy" calls on Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova T&D India, and CG Power and Industrial Solutions. articles.title: Indian-Americans behind 96 billion-dollar startups in US, new study challenges rising hate - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new study by the National Foundation for American Policy revealed that India leads in providing founders to the US, with 96 billion-dollar startups founded by Indian individuals. Despite recent social media narratives portraying Indian-Americans as job thieves, commentators praised their entrepreneurial spirit and contributions to the US economy.

articles.title: IndiGo Suspends Operations To 6 International Destinations
articles.rephrased_article: IndiGo, India's largest airline, has temporarily suspended operations to six international destinations, including Hong Kong and Krabi, starting July 1st. IndiGo will resume bookings for all impacted services on October 1st, subject to an improved environment. The carrier maintains over 1,800 weekly international flights despite this realignment.

articles.rephrased_article: Citigroup initiated "Buy" calls on Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova T&D India, and CG Power and Industrial Solutions, while maintaining a "Neutral" rating for Siemens Energy. articles.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit: Nilesh Shah recommends 4 investment bets that should be part of your portfolio - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: N.R. articles.title: UK firm DSP opens GCC in Bengaluru to deliver innovative solutions for global clients - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DSP, a UK-based enterprise database management company, opened its first overseas Global Capability Centre (GCC) in Bengaluru. articles.title: No more late salaries? UAE sees 151% jump in payroll processing as private-sector firms rush to meet new deadline - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UAE authorities have implemented a new wage payment rule requiring private sector employers to pay salaries on the first day of each month. This change, outlined in Ministerial Resolution No. 340 of 2026, has led to a significant increase in payroll processing activity across the private sector.  The UAE Central Bank and Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) jointly oversee the Wage Protection System (WPS), designed to ensure timely wage payments and strengthen compliance monitoring. The new rule has impacted small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) requiring them to adapt their cash flow planning and payroll schedules.  The implementation is part of broader UAE efforts to strengthen labour market governance, safeguard employee rights, and standardize wage payment practices across the private sector.

articles.title: India’s growth story remains strong, long-term outlook intact: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Jane Fraser, Chair of the Board and CEO of Citi, reaffirmed her confidence in India's long-term economic prospects, despite current global challenges.
