articles.title: Mutual funds avoid Rajesh Exports in last 10 years, LIC stake rose five times to 11% | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rajesh Exports, a gold and jewellery exporter, has been under scrutiny from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for allegedly inflating revenues over the past several years. articles.title: Market wrap: Sensex closes flat, Nifty holds 23,400; Titan, Eternal lead gains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex closed at 74,360, up nearly 14 points, while the Nifty 50 ended at 23,417, unchanged from the previous session. articles.title: Jet fuel price freeze: How the Rs 10,000-cr scheme affects airfares and airlines
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government has implemented a fixed price jet fuel scheme for participating airlines to stabilize airfares amid high international prices. The scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet, will see OMCs sell fuel at a fixed rate irrespective of market fluctuations, with losses being compensated from a stabilization fund.  This temporary arrangement is expected to ease financial pressure on both Indian airlines and OMCs for up to three years.

articles.title: Quantum Computing Is Having Its Public Market Moment | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Quantinuum, a quantum computer maker, is set to debut on the New York Stock Exchange this week despite facing financial challenges and skepticism about its technology's commercial viability. The company has seen significant revenue decline and lost nearly $200 million last year.  Despite these concerns, investor demand for Quantinuum shares has surged, leading to an increase in the price and number of shares being issued. This surge in interest is fueled by the growing popularity of quantum computing and a recent government investment in the field.

articles.title: Hero MotoCorp shares rise 3% as firm unveils India's first 100cc flex-fuel motorcycles. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hero MotoCorp, India's largest two-wheeler manufacturer, launched flex-fuel versions of its flagship Splendor+ and HF Deluxe motorcycles. The new models are compatible with ethanol-blended fuels ranging from E20 to E85 and aim to reduce carbon footprint while aligning with India's goal of lowering economic carbon intensity by 45% by 2030.  The launch was unveiled in New Delhi ahead of World Environment Day, attended by Union Ministers Nitin Gadkari and Hardeep Singh Puri, as well as Harshavardhan Chitale, CEO of Hero MotoCorp. The motorcycles will be available in select regions of Maharashtra and Delhi from July 2026.

articles.title: 'No Revenue Inflation': Rajesh Exports Rejects Rs 15 Lakh Crore Scam Charge
articles.rephrased_article: Rajesh Exports, a gold refining and jewelry giant, has denied allegations of Rs 15.15 lakh crore revenue inflation by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The company claims a communication gap caused the misunderstanding with SEBI and insists its revenues are accurate.  The Bengaluru-based company is submitting additional documents to the regulator and believes the investigation will clear up the concerns raised.  SEBI's interim order, which barred Rajesh Mehta from buying or selling securities of the company, has triggered a selloff in Rajesh Exports shares.

articles.title: Reliance traders said to game plan in case RBI raises rates - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance, one of India's largest conglomerates, is considering shifting its cash holdings from liquid mutual funds to short-dated money market instruments. This strategy aims to capitalize on the widening yield spread between money-market papers and benchmark rates, which is expected to narrow in the coming months. The conglomerate also discussed reducing allocations to longer-dated bonds due to their sensitivity to interest rate changes. Reliance's traders anticipate a stronger rupee if a Middle East peace deal occurs and the RBI takes measures to attract capital inflows.

articles.title: US economy remains strong, India must accelerate reforms and AI adoption: Ajay Srivastava - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Srivastava, an economic expert, believes the U.S. economy is strong and resilient despite geopolitical tensions. articles.title: Audio book platform Kuku files confidential papers for up to Rs 3,500-cr IPO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kuku Technologies, a company specializing in audio and video content, is planning to raise between Rs 2,500-Rs 3,500 crore through an IPO. articles.title: ICICI Bank shares fall 10% in 6 months. Here’s why Motilal Oswal sees 41% upside potential - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Bank shares gained over 1% on Thursday, trading at Rs 1,258.40 apiece, despite a recent decline in value. The brokerage expects a gradual rerating of ICICI Bank shares, maintaining its "Buy" call with a target price of Rs 1,750 apiece.

articles.title: Jefferies initiates coverage on Poonawalla Fincorp with Buy rating. Why are analysts bullish? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferies analysts are optimistic about Poonawalla Fincorp's future growth, citing its revamped leadership team, expanded product portfolio, and improved credit quality. articles.title: UBS downgrades BHEL shares to Neutral from Buy. Check target, key reasons - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: UBS downgraded its rating on BHEL stock, citing increased competition in the industry. articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) barred Rajesh Exports and its promoter-chairman, Rajesh Mehta, from accessing the securities market due to allegations of massive revenue misrepresentation spanning five financial years. articles.title: US plans additional 12.5% tariff; India says talks on Section 301 probes ongoing - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) proposed new tariffs on most Indian goods, citing concerns about forced labor and excess industrial capacity. The proposed tariffs would affect a wide range of products, but certain sectors like textiles and pharmaceuticals are excluded. articles.title: Aditya Shah favors domestic growth themes, stays bullish on IT and infrastructure sector - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shah, a prominent investor, advises focusing on EPC contractors, road contractors, and established players like L&T in the infrastructure sector due to strong order books. articles.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX IPO, priced at $135 per share, could make him world’s 1st trillionaire | Business News - The Indian Express

articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket company, is aiming for a valuation of nearly $1.77 trillion in its blockbuster initial public offering (IPO), seeking to raise approximately $75 billion by selling 555.6 million shares at $135 apiece. articles.rephrased_article: The Union Cabinet, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved an ordinance amending the Income Tax Act to eliminate capital gains tax on investments made by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in Indian government securities. articles.title: Indonesia’s rupiah falls to record low against US dollar | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesia’s rupiah has reached its record low against the US dollar, breaching 18,000, due to surging energy costs caused by the Iran-US war. articles.title: Kerala faces burden of ₹5.07-lakh crore liabilities; fiscal structure under ‘serious’ strain, says White Paper tabled by CM - The Hindu

articles.title: Rupee falls amidst gulf tensions and rising oil prices - The Economic Times

articles.title: IRCTC reinforces its AI monitoring system to ensure hygiene and quality of food in trains | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: IRCTC, the Indian Railways Catering and Tourism Corporation, has expanded its AI-based food hygiene monitoring system to over 800 kitchens. articles.title: Electric vehicles: Costly fuel pushes more Indians to buy EVs yet obstacles remain

articles.title: Why Canada has generic Ozempic, and the US doesn't
articles.rephrased_article: Canada became the first G7 country to approve a generic semaglutide injection, intended for type 2 diabetes patients but can be prescribed off-label for weight loss. The discounted medications are expected to be available in pharmacies across Canada as of June, at less than a third of the cost of brand-name drugs. The arrival of generics has prompted Novo Nordisk to lower prices of its brand-name drugs, but the company maintains that the situation in the US is different and it will continue to fight for its patent rights.

articles.title: CREDAI discusses with CM Vijay issues concerning real estate sector in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay
articles.rephrased_article: CREDAI, the Confederation of Real Estate Developers Associations of India, met with Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to discuss issues affecting the state's real estate sector. The delegation highlighted concerns regarding delays in approvals and requested a streamlined single-window system for faster project execution. They also raised concerns about the Ramsar designation on Pallikaranai Marsh, impacting landowners and hindering access to financial services. CREDAI proposed scrapping the designation or establishing a committee to complete the notification process within 30 days.  They further advocated for expanding the scope of self-certification and automatic building approval systems under the single-window mechanism.

articles.title: An app to help eateries sell surplus food - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kozhikode entrepreneurs Muhammed Nihal V. and Hiba Nourin K.P. are launching an app called Kyka, which connects eateries with customers to sell surplus food at discounted prices. The app, available on Google Play and the App Store from June 10th, operates on a "triple impact model" that reduces food waste, generates revenue for restaurants, and provides affordable meals for consumers.  The Kozhikode Corporation is supporting the initiative, which will initially operate in Kozhikode before expanding to other locations in Kerala and potentially beyond.

articles.title: PM Narendra Modi to launch, lay stone for infra initiatives worth Rs 18K crore in Surat tomorrow | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone for several development projects in Surat, Gujarat, worth over Rs 18,000 crore. These initiatives include four National Highway projects, two packages of the Vadodara–Mumbai Expressway, eight GIDC projects, and upgrades to the Hazira Port–Surat section of National Highway 53. The projects aim to strengthen connectivity, boost economic development, and improve freight movement along the Delhi–Mumbai expressway.

articles.title: What is the St Petersburg forum, Putin’s economic outreach to the world? | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Ukrainian drone strike near St. Petersburg disrupted operations at the city's airport hours before the start of the St Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF). The annual event, often called "Russia's Davos," is expected to attract 20,000 guests from over 130 countries and features discussions on topics such as energy markets, artificial intelligence, and information warfare.  President Vladimir Putin, who typically attends the forum, will deliver a keynote address outlining Russia's economic priorities and foreign policy ambitions. Rodney Mims Cook Jr., chairman of the US Commission of Fine Arts, is among the notable attendees representing the United States. The forum also features representatives from countries like Uzbekistan, Tanzania, China, Saudi Arabia, and Belarus.  The event serves as a platform for Moscow to showcase its economic resilience amidst Western sanctions and promote international partnerships beyond the West.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow Jones drops over 500 points as Middle East tensions escalate - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all closed in negative territory on Tuesday, dragged lower by financials and tech.  While the artificial intelligence sector showed resilience, concerns over geopolitical tensions and inflation persisted. The Middle East hostilities intensified, oil prices rose, and the Federal Reserve's December meeting rate hike probability increased. Despite positive economic data, corporate spending plans appeared soft amid rising energy costs.

articles.title: SpaceX Aims To Raise Record $75 Billion In Stock Market Debut: Report
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the rocket and satellite company led by Elon Musk, plans to raise approximately $75 billion through a record-breaking initial public offering (IPO). The company will sell 555,555,555 shares at an initial price of $135 each. This move would surpass the previous record held by Saudi Aramco, which raised $25.6 billion in 2019.

articles.title: Amazon Employees Show Up to City Council Meeting to Demand Limits on Data Centers | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Two Amazon employees, Liesl Wigand and Patrick Schloesser, publicly urged Seattle officials to regulate new data center construction, citing environmental, economic, and safety concerns. They advocated for increased renewable energy use, power storage, and worker-led safety committees.  The comments mark a significant escalation in the nationwide protest against rapid data center development, with workers from various tech companies expressing similar concerns. Amazon did not immediately comment on the employees' statements. Seattle is considering a one-year pause on issuing permits for new data centers to establish regulations.

articles.title: Thali costs climb in May: Crisil report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Crisil predicts elevated tomato, potato, and onion prices in the coming months due to lower production and supply constraints. Tomato prices are expected to remain high through June-August as summer sowing is impacted by heat concerns in key growing states.  Potato prices will also increase as the rabi harvest season concludes. On the other hand, Crisil expects pulses prices to remain subdued due to ample domestic availability.

articles.title: The Great Chinese Factory Glut Is Starting To Choke The World
articles.rephrased_article: China's total non-financial sector debt has reached 313% of GDP and is projected to reach 323% by 2026. This rising debt, coupled with declining efficiency of investment, suggests a weakening growth model that relies heavily on capital formation rather than household demand.  The country's property slowdown, falling land sales, and demographic decline are exacerbating the situation. IMF estimates show China is operating with a negative output gap and core inflation remains low. This economic imbalance has led to an oversupply of goods in export markets, particularly electric vehicles and solar panels, which are flooding global markets despite tariffs.  The "New Three" sectors - electric vehicles, batteries, and solar manufacturing - reflect this struggle for domestic demand.

articles.title: Cabinet Approves Rs 10,000-Crore Fund Amid Rising Jet Fuel Prices
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government approved a Rs 10,000 crore aviation fuel price stabilization fund to mitigate the impact of rising global prices.  Information Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that the fund will help stabilize aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices for airlines and prevent disruptions in operations. The fund is expected to protect 77 lakh jobs dependent on the aviation ecosystem and safeguard public investment in airport infrastructure. It will be in effect for 36 months, with annual reviews or until the advance amount is fully recovered/settled.

articles.title: We expect interest rates to be left the way they are: Ficci chief Anant Goenka - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RPG Group's vice-chairman, Goenka, expressed optimism about India's economic future despite concerns over foreign capital outflows. He advocated for continued ease of doing business and a focus on key sectors like data centers and semiconductors, while acknowledging the impact of the West Asia conflict on GDP growth. Goenka also emphasized the importance of leveraging free trade agreements (FTAs) to boost manufacturing and highlighted that recent market corrections have led to FPIs returning. He believes India's markets are now more fairly valued after a period of overvaluation.

articles.title: We expect interest rates to be left the way they are: Ficci chief Anant Goenka - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RPG Group vice-chairman, Goenka, expressed optimism about India's economic outlook despite concerns over foreign capital outflows and potential GDP impact from the West Asia conflict. He advocated for maintaining current interest rates and minimizing rupee intervention while emphasizing the need to leverage free trade agreements (FTAs) and focus on key sectors like data centers and semiconductors. Goenka also noted that recent corrections in Indian markets may lead to a return of foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).

articles.title: Norms issued to estimate District Domestic Product - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has released guidelines recommending the use of various data sources to estimate economic activity in different sectors. These include GST collections for trade, hotels, and restaurants; Annual Survey of Industries data for organized manufacturing; Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises for informal sector activities; and RBI banking statistics for financial services. The guidelines also reflect the recent revision of the national gross domestic product (GDP) base year to 2022-23. These recommendations aim to support evidence-based policy formulation, regional development analysis, and informed decision-making at the district level.

articles.title: RBI likely to hold rates as West Asia crisis impact on growth remains unclear: Bank of Baroda Report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to maintain interest rates on Friday, June 5th, as the impact of the ongoing West Asia crisis on economic growth remains unclear. The central bank will likely continue its data-dependent approach, balancing growth concerns with inflation risks and global uncertainties.  Bank of Baroda, a financial institution, anticipates an upward revision in RBI's CPI projection for FY27 due to rising fuel prices and expects the RBI to retain its neutral policy stance.

articles.title: ADB, StanChart ink partnership to support Indian firms across supply chains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Standard Chartered Bank have signed agreements to strengthen supply chain finance in India. The agreements, including a risk participation arrangement through Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City) and a partial guarantee facility agreement, aim to expand access to trade and supply chain finance for businesses operating in India. These arrangements are intended to support the continued flow of cross-border and domestic trade, particularly by addressing financing gaps for emerging and underserved segments like distributor financing, which often involves small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This partnership aligns with ADB's strategic priority to promote inclusive economic growth and financial deepening across Asia and the Pacific.

articles.title: Jefferies raises Titagarh Rail target price by 23%. Check upside potential and key triggers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferies raised its target for Titagarh Rail Systems, citing strong execution and a robust order book. The brokerage believes the company is well-positioned to benefit from rising demand for passenger and metro coaches, supported by government infrastructure initiatives.  Titagarh Rail Systems delivered 64 coaches in FY26, ahead of expectations, and expects to deliver 200-220 coaches in FY27. The brokerage forecasts a 44% EPS CAGR over FY26-30, with margins expected to improve gradually towards 15%.

articles.title: Ronaldo, Taylor Swift and Mickey Mouse are fighting for your attention
articles.rephrased_article: A study by IPAM, Portugal's marketing institute, found that hosting the 2026 World Cup would generate an estimated 945 million euros in economic impact, even if Portugal does not advance beyond the group stage.  The digital component of the event now accounts for 23% of the total impact, with domestic consumption and traditional revenue sources like betting and merchandising still significant contributors. Daniel Sá, IPAM's executive director, emphasized the need for a comprehensive strategy that leverages the digital ecosystem to enhance Portugal's visibility and leave a lasting legacy beyond the tournament itself.

articles.title: ₹7,597-crore NH upgradation project approved for Telangana, to boost regional connectivity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central government approved a ₹7,597 crore national highway upgradation project for four-laning of 190.76 km stretch of the National Highway (NH)-63 and NH-563 in north Telangana. The project will widen the Armoor-Jagtial-Mancherial section of NH-63 to four-lane standards on HAM, and the Jagtial-Karimnagar section of NH-563 under BOT (Toll) Mode. This upgrade aims to reduce travel times between key cities and boost regional connectivity and economic growth.  Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar hailed the project as a game-changing infrastructure boost that will power the growth of Telangana for decades to come.

articles.title: Rajesh Exports: Sebi finds 97-99% revenue inflation, bars promoter from trading - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the market regulator, has issued an interim order against Rajesh Exports, a gold refiner and jewellery manufacturer, alleging that approximately 97-99% of its revenue may be inflated. The investigation, prompted by a shareholder complaint, found evidence of non-cooperation from the company and its promoter, including withholding financial records and refusing access to key accounting systems.  Sebi has restrained Rajesh Mehta, the company's promoter, from dealing in securities until further orders and directed the company to cooperate fully with investigators. The regulator also ordered a fresh forensic audit of the company's books and transactions.

articles.title: Market correction nearing its end; bet on banking, pharma: Rohit Srivastava - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Srivastava, a market expert, believes the Nifty is approaching a key technical support zone that could signal an end to the current correction. He suggests investors consider banking stocks as they show relative resilience compared to other sectors and have experienced a divergence from the broader market decline.  The energy sector and metals are also seen as potential areas for investment due to improving commodity trends. While the auto sector is consolidating, Srivastava believes pharmaceuticals present a strong long-term outlook with a recent technical breakout.

articles.title: IndusInd Bank shares fall 3% after fresh whistleblower complaint reaches PMO, RBI - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A whistleblower has filed a complaint alleging insider trading and financial irregularities at IndusInd Bank, including manipulation of financial records, evergreening of microfinance loans, suppression of audit findings, and attempts to conceal irregularities. The complaint also alleges that former zonal head of eastern India, Samir Agarwal, generated significant profits through share transactions using confidential information.  IndusInd Bank has denied the allegations, stating they have been thoroughly examined and appropriate actions taken in line with internal policies and regulatory requirements.

articles.title: ITC shares fall 3% to fresh 52-week low; Motilal Oswal sees more pain ahead - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ITC shares dropped to a 52-week low on Wednesday, following the decline of IT stocks.  Motilal Oswal Financial Services attributed the drop to the implementation of GST 2.0, which has resulted in significant increases in cigarette taxes for ITC. The brokerage expects volatility in ITC's cigarette business due to the tax hikes and anticipates a 15% revenue decline and a 19% dip in earnings for FY27.  However, they also highlight the positive performance of ITC's non-cigarette businesses.

articles.title: As El Niño threatens monsoon, farmer groups promote millets, mulching and drip irrigation | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Agriculture is working to support farmers facing challenges from a weak southwest monsoon by promoting drought-resistant crops and climate-resilient farming practices. The ministry has identified farmer-producer organizations (FPOs) across the country that are cultivating drought-resistant crops like millets, and is holding webinars to educate farmers on these methods.  The Ministry plans to use the network of over 63 lakh farmers from 10,000 FPOs to encourage adoption of climate-resilient practices, including alternative crops and moisture conservation techniques.

articles.title: Indians run some of the world's biggest companies. Why do we build so few of them?
articles.rephrased_article: Indian leaders are increasingly prominent in global corporations, but the article argues that this success stems from a highly competitive environment rather than inherent intelligence or cultural factors.  The pressure to succeed within India's social and economic system fosters resilience and discipline, qualities valued by large organizations. This high-pressure talent filter produces individuals who excel at managing complexity and enduring uncertainty, characteristics often overlooked in discussions about leadership. However, the article cautions that this relentless pressure can also lead to burnout and discourage creativity. The focus should shift from simply supplying CEOs to creating a system that fosters both resilience and innovation.

articles.title: Eternal to ICICI Bank: 15 stocks on Axis Securities buy list for June - Add to cart | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Axis Securities has recommended 15 stocks across various market segments for June, expecting upside potential of up to 44% in its top picks. The brokerage maintains a positive outlook on India's macroeconomic fundamentals despite global challenges like higher crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions. Axis Securities believes investors should use market corrections to accumulate quality companies with strong earnings visibility.  The brokerage favors banking, telecom, capital goods, healthcare, power, and energy sectors while also recommending select consumption and capex-linked businesses.

articles.title: Stop Chasing Returns, Build Portfolio That Pays Monthly Salary. Here's How
articles.rephrased_article: Ajay Kumar Yadav, Group CEO & CIO of Wise Finserv, emphasizes that the focus for retirees and those nearing retirement should shift from wealth accumulation to generating consistent monthly income.  Experts advise against relying on a single product like fixed deposits or mutual funds, recommending instead a diversified portfolio combining instruments such as annuities, SWPs, Balanced Advantage Funds, and growth assets.  Anisha Kathotia, an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor, suggests that these strategies can create a stable income stream while also allowing for long-term growth. Ajay Kumar Yadav stresses the importance of considering post-tax returns and inflation when evaluating investment options, advocating for moderation in withdrawals to ensure the portfolio's sustainability over time.

articles.title: What’s Worth More Than Cash in San Francisco Real Estate? Anthropic Stock | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Swann, a listing agent in San Francisco, is offering a unique real estate option: buyers can purchase a home at 160 Noe Street by exchanging their Anthropic or OpenAI stock. This unconventional approach stems from the high valuations of these companies and the desire to capitalize on potential future growth. Several individuals have proposed similar exchanges, including an investment banker who offered his Mill Valley property for Anthropic shares, and a real estate owner in Healdsburg who listed his home with a $500,000 discount in exchange for Anthropic stock.  While some experts consider these transactions unconventional and potentially illegal, the listings have garnered attention from potential buyers and investors alike.

articles.title: Vodafone Idea shares rally 7% to fresh 52-week high despite market crash. What's behind the surge? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone Idea’s stock has experienced significant growth, with its market capitalization exceeding Rs 1.62 lakh crore.  The ratings agency ICRA upgraded the company's rating to A- from BBB and revised its outlook on long-term fund-based loans to 'Stable'. This upgrade was driven by support from the Aditya Birla Group, including the re-appointment of Kumar Mangalam Birla as Chairman and a proposed equity infusion.  Citi Research removed its 'High Risk' rating and raised its target price for the stock, citing positive factors like government AGR dues reassessment and increased financial flexibility.

articles.title: Zirakpur Penthouse dispute: Consumer panel orders against Barnala builders | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
articles.sentiment_target: Barnala Builder and Property Consultants Developers
articles.rephrased_article: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) in Mohali, Punjab, ruled in favor of retired Army officer Colonel Romesh Ghai and his daughter Shaheen Ghai against Barnala Builder and Property Consultants Developers. The commission ordered the builder to refund excess charges, provide promised amenities, compensate for delays in obtaining necessary approvals, and pay litigation expenses.  The Commission also directed the builder to obtain Completion and Occupation Certificates from competent authorities and deliver them to the complainants.

articles.title: CMR Green Tech’s Rs 630 cr IPO opens for bidding: Check GMP, brokerages review and other details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: CMR Green Technologies, India's largest non-ferrous metal recycler, is launching an IPO with a GMP of around 33%, suggesting a potential listing price of Rs 255-256 per share. The company will offer shares worth Rs 630.6 crore through an offer for sale (OFS) and has fixed a price band of Rs 182-192 per share, with investors able to bid for a minimum lot of 78 shares.  Analysts have offered mixed views on the IPO, with some highlighting the company's industry leadership and strong market position while others caution about its dependence on key clients and thin operating margins. Investors will closely watch subscription trends over the next three days to gauge demand from institutional and retail investors.

articles.title: AT&T Promo Codes: $50 Off This June 2026 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: AT&T offers various discounts and promotions for its wireless plans, including prepaid options, fiber internet, and bundled deals.  These include savings on new phones, family plans, and discounts for teachers, first responders, and students. The company also provides a 30-day free trial of its wireless service to allow customers to test the network before committing.

articles.title: Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc shares fall after metals giant confirms ED visits to offices - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta Group, a company led by Anil Agarwal, stated that its offices and those of its subsidiary, Hindustan Zinc, were visited by officials from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) as part of a Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) investigation. The company is cooperating with authorities and providing all requested information.  Vedanta Group also confirmed that proceedings are underway and reiterated its commitment to complying with applicable laws and regulations.

articles.title: TCS, Infosys, other IT stocks crash up to 7% after 3-day rally. What top brokerages are saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL Tech, and Tech Mahindra saw significant declines in stock prices following concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence on the software services industry.  Despite this, several brokerages remain optimistic about the long-term prospects of the sector, citing the resilience of earnings estimates and management guidance. They believe that companies with strong partnerships with SaaS providers will continue to benefit from demand for product engineering and implementation services. Nuvama Institutional Equities, Choice Institutional Equities, and BofA Securities have all pushed back against bearish narratives, arguing that Indian IT services are well-positioned to adapt to the evolving AI landscape.  However, foreign institutional investors remain unconvinced about the sector's resilience, continuing to sell off their holdings in 2025.

articles.title: TCS, Infosys, other IT stocks crash up to 7% after 3-day rally. What top brokerages are saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL Tech, and Tech Mahindra experienced significant declines following concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence on the software services industry. Despite these fears, several brokerages remain optimistic about the sector's long-term prospects, citing resilience in earnings estimates and management guidance. They argue that AI will enhance existing systems rather than replace them entirely, while also highlighting the growing demand for product engineering and implementation services from companies with strong partnerships with SaaS providers.  However, foreign institutional investors have continued to sell IT stocks, reflecting skepticism about the sector's ability to fully adapt to AI advancements.

articles.title: Concord Biotech jumps 8% on USFDA nod for Mycophenolate Mofetil oral suspension - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Concord Biotech announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) approval of its antimetabolite immunosuppressant, Mycophenolate Mofetil for Oral Suspension USP, 200 mg/mL, for organ rejection prophylaxis in adult and pediatric patients undergoing kidney, heart, or liver transplants. The company expects this approval to strengthen its presence in the U.S. pharmaceutical market and generate significant commercial opportunities within a US$30 million market.  The approval was granted without any withdrawal, cancellation, or suspension of the product's status.

articles.title: Elon Musk Could Become World's First Trillionaire With SpaceX's Market Debut
articles.rephrased_article: Elon Musk, the world's richest man, is expected to become the planet's first trillionaire when SpaceX makes its highly anticipated stock market debut around June 12th. Forbes estimates his net worth at nearly $835 billion, surpassing Google co-founder Larry Page. The company's valuation is projected to range from $1.7 trillion to $2 trillion, with Musk holding approximately 42 percent of capital and 79 percent of voting rights after the public offering.  Experts warn that this concentration of wealth could lead to further societal inequality and instability.

articles.title: US proposes fresh 12.5% tariffs on India amid trade talks, 10% on Pak, Canada, EU | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Trade Representative (USTR) proposed 12.5% tariffs on India among 54 countries, citing the country's failure to enforce a ban on forced labor imports.  This move comes as formal trade negotiations between India and the US began on Tuesday. The USTR also proposed lower tariffs for other nations like Pakistan, Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, and Mexico, acknowledging their commitment to addressing forced labor imports. Public comment is being sought on these proposed actions, with a public hearing scheduled for July 7th.

articles.title: Sensex Today, Stock Market LIVE Updates | Nifty | Share Market: Sensex Drops 550 Points Amid Mixed Global Cues
articles.rephrased_article: Indian equity benchmarks opened in red on Wednesday, driven by escalating US-Iran tensions. The Sensex fell over 500 points and the Nifty was down 150 points.  RBI MPC, Crypto Update, and India-Oman Trade are among the topics being discussed.  The rupee weakened against the US dollar.

articles.title: Concord Biotech jumps 8% on USFDA nod for Mycophenolate Mofetil oral suspension - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Concord Biotech announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) approval of its antimetabolite immunosuppressant, Mycophenolate Mofetil for Oral Suspension USP, 200 mg/mL. The approval is expected to strengthen Concord Biotech's presence in the U.S. pharmaceutical market and generate significant commercial opportunities within the estimated US$30 million market. The company noted that the approval was granted without any withdrawal, cancellation, or suspension of the product, and did not result in any penalties or financial impact.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu deserves to have world-class airports: CII Chairman - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Ravichandran, Chairman of the CII Southern Region and President of Danfoss India, expressed his belief that Tamil Nadu deserves a top-tier airport, arguing that its current ranking is inadequate.  He stated that while there have been no discussions with the government regarding the Parandur airport project, the CII delegation met with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to discuss the importance of the facility for industry growth. Ravichandran emphasized that a well-functioning airport is crucial for attracting investors and ensuring efficient operations.

articles.title: South Western Railway sets new record in freight loading - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: South Western Railway (SWR) has broken its own record for originating freight loading, reaching 4.40 million tonnes in May 2026. The company achieved a 4.3% increase compared to the previous year and surpassed the previous record of 4.25 MT set in May 2008.  This growth was reflected in an average of 2,275 wagons loaded per day, representing a 3.7% increase from the same period last year.

articles.title: For larger PNG footprint, Government looks at consumer-friendly centralised portal | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government is proposing a centralized portal to facilitate the migration of LPG consumers to PNG. This move aims to ease pressure on LPG supplies due to disruptions in imports, particularly from West Asia. The proposal involves making gas grid maps publicly accessible and streamlining the application process for new PNG connections.  While the implementation timeline remains uncertain, the government has already issued orders directing households and commercial users to switch to PNG where available.

articles.title: Nifty IT logs best run in a year at 4%; TCS, Infosys lead way - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty IT index surged 4.2% on Tuesday, reaching its highest point since May 2025, driven by improving global software sentiment and growing enterprise AI adoption.  TCS, Infosys, HCL Technologies, and LTM were among the top performers, with analysts citing factors like rupee depreciation, strong orderbooks, and a positive outlook for discretionary tech spending as supporting this rally. While domestic IT stocks have underperformed the broader market in 2026, experts predict further gains for the sector, potentially reaching 32,000-32,100.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks end modestly higher as AI zeal overcomes Middle East jitters - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed higher on Tuesday, driven by gains in small-cap stocks and a surge in AI-related companies.  Hewlett Packard Enterprise saw its stock rise after it accelerated its financial targets, while Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion for its AI infrastructure expansion. However, the Nasdaq Composite remained essentially unchanged. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index advanced on the day, and analysts predict a potential "heated, melt-up rally" in the coming months.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks end modestly higher as AI zeal overcomes Middle East jitters - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed higher, driven by gains in small-cap stocks and a surge in AI-related companies.  While the Nasdaq Composite remained essentially unchanged, Hewlett Packard Enterprise saw its stock rise after it accelerated its financial targets, while Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion for its AI infrastructure expansion. The Labor Department reported an unexpected spike in job openings, fueled by the volatile professional and business services sector.  Analysts predict a slowdown in hiring and firing activity due to uncertainties related to the Middle East conflict and inflation.

articles.title: Billionaire Mark Cuban exposes American healthcare: Why one MRI costs $2,500 while another costs just $350 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Cuban sparked a debate about the high cost of healthcare in the US when he questioned why an MRI scan could cost $2,500 at an insurer-affiliated hospital while another facility nearby offered it for $350.  The discussion highlighted the complex pricing practices of hospitals and insurance companies, which often negotiate reimbursement rates that are significantly higher than independent imaging centers' prices. Healthcare experts point to factors like hospital chargemaster pricing, facility fees, and negotiated rates between insurers and providers as contributing to these price discrepancies. Cuban has long criticized healthcare pricing transparency, arguing that it makes it difficult for patients to compare costs and make informed decisions about their care.

articles.title: Chinese humanoids are one step closer to IPOs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Unitree Robotics, a leading robotics company, received approval for an IPO in Shanghai. This move signals a potential wave of robotic offerings in China, mirroring the rapid growth of its AI ecosystem and Beijing's push to prioritize industrial deployment.  The IPO is expected to raise funds for research and development, particularly robot models, with companies like Leju Robotics and Deep Robotics also filing applications. While some investors remain cautious about valuations potentially exceeding earnings, others see the sector as a long-term growth opportunity due to advancements in AI.

articles.title: Iran inflation hits highest level since World War II. Is another crisis brewing? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's annual inflation rate surged to 77.2% in May, marking the highest level since World War II and reflecting a deepening economic crisis. The Iranian Central Bank reported monthly inflation of 8.5% compared with April, with prices for essential goods like medicine and communication services rising significantly. Economists attribute the surge to war-related disruptions, US sanctions, and years of economic mismanagement.  President Masoud Pezeshkian warned citizens that further price increases are likely, while some analysts predict inflation could reach 80% in coming months. This escalating economic situation has raised concerns about potential social unrest.

articles.title: 10 stocks with over 10% mutual funds ownership and strong QoQ stake growth - ​Mutual Fund Favorites | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mutual funds increased their holdings in several companies within the BSE 500 universe, with some seeing significant growth.  Among these companies, Sarda Energy & Minerals, Chennai Petroleum Corporation, and Waaree Energies saw notable increases in mutual fund ownership. However, despite this increase, mutual funds still held less than 3% of each company. The article highlights the performance of ten stocks that have seen substantial increases in mutual fund holdings and price performance.
